passages.original: Equidem, Beatissime Pater, cum plura ejuscemodi monumenta non desint, quibus Brixiana Ecclesia mirum in modum decoratur, præclarissimum illud est, quod in ejus cathedra præsules quatuor sederunt, sanctitate æque editis Scriptis illustres, quorum duo, Sancti scilicet, Philastrius, et Gaudentius, divi Augustini Hipponensis episcopi ætalem attigerunt, Beatus vero Rampertus a nonagentis, ac venerabilis Adelmannus a septingentis circiter annis florueruat. Porro Philastrius suppar adeo fuit Augustino, ut hic a Quotvultdeo diacono per epistolam rogatus tractatum de Hæresibus conscribere, Philastrium sibi notum Mediolani apud Ambrosium, id ipsum abunde præstitisse respon- derit. Gaudentius autem eo ipso Mediolanensium sanctissimo Præsule satagente, dum in Oriente ad sacra Loca peregrinaretur, Brixianam Ecclesiam florenti adhuc ætate sibi delatam accepit.
passages.english: Indeed, Most Blessed Father, though there is no lack of many monuments of this kind by which the Church of Brescia is wonderfully adorned, the most illustrious is this: that four prelates sat in its see who were distinguished alike for holiness and for the writings they published. Two of them, namely Saints Philastrius and Gaudentius, reached the age of the divine Augustine, bishop of Hippo, while Blessed Rampertus flourished about nine hundred years ago, and the Venerable Adelmannus about seven hundred. Philastrius was so nearly contemporary with Augustine that when Augustine was asked by letter by the deacon Quodvultdeus to write a treatise on heresies, he replied that Philastrius, whom he had known at Milan in the company of Ambrose, had already done this very thing abundantly. Gaudentius, for his part, through the efforts of that same most holy prelate of the Milanese, received the Church of Brescia, which was conferred on him while he was still in the prime of life, at the time when he was on pilgrimage to the holy places in the East.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'ætalem' read as 'ætatem', 'florueruat' as 'floruerunt', 'respon- derit' as 'responderit'. 'Quotvultdeo' is the edition's spelling of the deacon Quodvultdeus.
